paper_id: Placement is not Enough_ Embedding with Proactive Stream Mapping on the Heterogenous Edge
title: Placement is not Enough: Embedding with Proactive Stream Mapping on the Heterogenous Edge
motivation: IoT stream processing on edge requires low latency; existing approaches only optimize function placement passively.
problem_framing: Joint optimization of function placement and stream mapping with data splitting on heterogeneous edge to minimize DAG makespan.
key_insight: Proactive stream mapping and data splitting can significantly reduce makespan even when function placement appears suboptimal.
method_signature: Dynamic programming-based embedding (DPE) solving function embedding substructure optimally.
evaluation_criteria: Makespan reduction vs FixDoc and HEFT on Alibaba cluster trace with 2119 DAGs.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Complexity O(N!) is of great order; offline algorithm sacrifices runtime for global optimality.
thinking_moves: Identify that routing path is passive (SDN-generated) vs should be optimized
Decompose joint placement+mapping problem via optimal substructure in DP
Transform infinity norm minimization to LP via slack variables
Prove optimal condition via AM-GM inequality to avoid simplex method
Acknowledge NP-hard path enumeration while accepting offline runtime cost
cites_own_work: FixDoc (Liu et al. 2019) is compared as baseline
extraction_notes: Shuiguang Deng appears as co-author with equal contribution marker but not explicitly marked as corresponding. Year not explicitly stated in paper; inferred from arxiv ID 2012.xxxxx as 2020.
